decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives x^3(ln(x))^2/3 − (2/3)[x^3 ln(x)/3 − x^3/9] + C = x^3[9(ln(x))^2 − 6ln(x) + 2]/27 + C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x))(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}(\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}+D) \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}{3}-\frac{2{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{9}+\frac{2{x}^{3}}{27}-\frac{2D}{3} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{27}(9(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{3}.$

after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+1)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(10x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }5{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-(5{\pi }^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +10\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +10\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -(-(5(0)^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡0))-10\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡0-10\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =5{\pi }^{2}+1-10+1-10 \\  & =5{\pi }^{2}-18\end{aligned}
$$

$$
